clue.text: Means to examine semi-homespun cotton twisted into yarn?

indicators.note: into means the shuffled letters are put inside the word for yarn

parts.note: a yarn is a tall story, a fib

indicators.note: twisted means the letters are wound into a new order
semi- means half, so only the first half of homespun is used

explanation.surface: A rustic textile question: what you get by twisting half-homespun cotton into yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-' gives HOME, the first half of homespun; 'twisted' shuffles HOME plus COTTON into NETOOTHCOM, which goes 'into' FIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A comb with closely set teeth is the proverbial tool for a meticulous search, so it is a means to examine minutely.

clue.text: Ditch rich for going first — this is amusing

indicators.note: the word for rich is said to go first, ahead of the ditch

parts.note: 'that's rich' means that's funny, so rich can mean funny
a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a fence in a landscaped park

explanation.surface: A dig at the wealthy: swapping riches for a ditch is the comic part.
explanation.walkthrough: A HA-HA is a ditch hidden in a British country-house garden that keeps livestock out without blocking the view.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase distinguishes humorous funniness from the peculiar kind, so it means comical or laughable.

clue.text: Nicks records about church

indicators.note: about means the word for records goes around the church abbreviation

parts.note: notes are written records

explanation.surface: Someone pinches records from around a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cuts or indentations made in an edge are nicks, synonyms for the plural noun.

clue.text: See 1
Slightly devious tone two universities initially misconstrued beforehand

indicators.note: beforehand means the rearranged letters are placed ahead of the word for devious
misconstrued means these letters are read wrongly, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: two means the initial letter of universities is used twice
initially means only the first letter of universities is taken

parts.note: devious means sly

explanation.surface: An academic complains that a crafty tone from two universities was misread in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two universities initially' gives UU; 'misconstrued' turns TONE plus UU into TENUOU, placed 'beforehand' of SLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held only weakly or in a flimsy way is held slightly, the adverb's sense of thin connection.

clue.text: Bound dictionary with large content — with large content

indicators.note: the dictionary has the following material as its content, holding it inside

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: the word for large itself holds the abbreviation for large as its content

parts.note: large means big
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A bound dictionary with lots of content, the phrase repeated as if for emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition is the trick: the first 'with large content' puts BIG inside O_ED, the second puts L inside BIG to make BLIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bound to do something means being compelled or duty-bound, a synonym in the passive sense.

clue.text: Article supporting back-to-back housing causing fuss

indicators.note: in a down clue the article goes beneath, holding up the housing letters

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house; one HO followed by a reversed HO puts two houses back to back
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on terraced back-to-back housing stirs up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Back-to-back houses are British terraced homes sharing a rear wall; here HO and its reversal OH meet back to back.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or noisy fuss over nothing much is a hullabaloo, the sense of this informal word.

clue.text: See 1
In bed, sick, leader perhaps going over dance

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
sick means ill

indicators.note: going over means the letters for the leader are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a leader is number one, NO 1, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A leader laid up sick in bed misses the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader perhaps' is NO 1, number one, written NOI; 'going over' reverses it to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An eighteenth-century French formal dance for couples in sets, ancestor of the quadrille.

clue.text: Knight taking turn to follow horse in battle

indicators.note: to follow means these letters come after the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: taking means the knight picks up the turn beside it

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
a turn, as in 'your go', is a go

explanation.surface: A chess knight makes its move, following a horse into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon's horse was also named after this battle, which makes 'horse in battle' a neat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon defeated the Austrians at this village in northern Italy in 1800, a famous battle.

clue.text: Draw country animal, penned by friend

parts.note: a nation is a country

indicators.note: penned by means the animal is enclosed within the word for friend

parts.note: an ally is a friend
the otter is an animal

explanation.surface: A farm scene: a country animal kept in a pen by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb but is the noun, a prize draw; the UK's state-run lottery is the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw of numbers for prizes; the national one is the UK's main such draw.

clue.text: Pleb embracing British 'up yours!'

indicators.note: embracing means the word for pleb holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: a yahoo is a coarse, uncultured person, from Swift

explanation.surface: A lout hugs a Briton while shouting a rude insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are childish jeering exclamations of contempt or defiance, so the interjections match.

clue.text: Galileo worked outside new boundary

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters sit around the abbreviation
worked means the letters are worked into a new shape, an anagram

explanation.surface: Galileo laboured beyond the frontiers of new knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or rugby the line at each end of the pitch marks the edge of play, a boundary.

clue.text: Scientist is dissecting fag-ends regularly dropped by climber, say

indicators.note: dissecting means cutting into the picked letters, sitting inside them
regularly means every other letter of fag-ends is taken, here the even ones

parts.note: a BSc is a Bachelor of Science, so a scientist by degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scientist cuts up cigarette ends, which a climber drops.
explanation.walkthrough: The climber is a climbing plant, not a mountaineer; 'regularly' takes A, E, D from fag-ends, which BSC IS is 'dissecting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants shed leaves or fruit by abscission, so parts dropped by a plant such as a climber are cast off this way.

clue.text: History student admitted to dreadful English

indicators.note: admitted to means the student goes inside the following letters

parts.note: chronic is informal British for dreadful, very bad
L is a learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A history student is let in to some dreadful English.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a factual record of events in order, a written account of the past.

clue.text: Almost hide diamonds and rings in specialist transport

indicators.note: almost means the word for hide loses its last letter

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
rings are round shapes, two Os

explanation.surface: Someone almost conceals diamonds and rings in a special vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorised snow vehicle is a snowmobile, a specialist form of transport for icy terrain.

clue.text: Mixed drink and drug consumed by jiving beatniks

indicators.note: consumed by means the drug is swallowed inside the rearranged letters
jiving means dancing about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Dancing beatniks take a mixed drink and a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jiving' shuffles BEATNIKS, which has E 'consumed by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub drink combining lager and cider in one glass, a mixed drink popular in Britain.

clue.text: Exceeds with cracking cryptic Toughies

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into the rearranged letters, sitting inside them
cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are disguised in a new order

explanation.surface: A boast that these cryptic Toughies exceed others, with cracking quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' shuffles TOUGHIES, which W goes into, 'cracking' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be heavier or more important than something is to surpass it, a synonym.

clue.text: I am ready, ignoring the odds, to accept following fight

indicators.note: to accept means the remaining letters take the abbreviation inside
ignoring the odds means the odd letters of the phrase are dropped, leaving the even ones

parts.note: ff is the abbreviation for 'and the following' pages

explanation.surface: A boxer declares readiness to take on all comers in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring the odds' leaves ARAY from I AM READY; it is said 'to accept' FF.
explanation.definitionFit: A public brawl or disturbance of the peace is a fight, especially in legal usage.

clue.text: 'Director once collapsed', one added

indicators.note: added means the numeral is joined on at the end

parts.note: a roof that collapsed fell in
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A headline quote, 'Director once collapsed', with one more fact added.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was the Italian film director of La Dolce Vita, who died in 1993.

clue.text: Note in passage by W H Auden, originally and now?

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of Auden is used
in means the note's letter goes inside the passage

parts.note: a passage of writing is a text

explanation.surface: A query on a note in a passage by the poet W H Auden: and now?
explanation.walkthrough: W H is read as written; 'originally' gives the A of Auden.
explanation.definitionFit: Both ask in exasperation or anticipation what is to come after this, so the question means the same.

clue.text: Fish scrap in bottom of bag

parts.note: a whit is a tiny scrap, as in 'not a whit'

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fish scrap lies at the bottom of the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiting is a small food fish of the cod family, common in North Atlantic waters.

clue.text: In city, Castro nearly set up complex organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the letters are raised, read upwards

parts.note: EC1 is a postcode in the City of London, written with I for 1

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Fidel was the first name of Cuba's leader Castro

explanation.surface: In some city, Castro nearly established a complicated organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is the City of London via its postcode EC1, three characters; 'set up' reverses EC1 plus FIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is figuratively a large, elaborate system or structure, such as an institution.

clue.text: Evil woman left heart in Wales back here?

indicators.note: back means the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: evil means ill, as in ill will
Ena is a woman's name

indicators.note: the heart in a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: An evil woman left her heart in Wales and must come back.
explanation.walkthrough: Llanelli is a town in South Wales, so 'here?' points to a place, hinted by Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark marks a place clued by example: a town on the south Welsh coast.

clue.text: Girl caught in blind alley

indicators.note: caught in means the name is trapped within the letters of blind alley

explanation.surface: A girl is trapped in a dead end.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a girl's given name, so a girl clued by example.

clue.text: Major organisation of a republic blocked by member

indicators.note: blocked by means the republic has the member stuck inside it

parts.note: Eire is the Irish Republic
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A major body of a republic is obstructed by one of its members.
explanation.definitionFit: A large business group run by one person is called a commercial empire, a big organisation.

clue.text: Thermal controller in dining car too erratic — I should stop it

indicators.note: should stop it means the letter I plugs a gap inside the jumbled letters
erratic means behaving unpredictably, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A passenger complains that the dining car's climate system is erratic and wants it stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sits in the fodder, not the link: 'erratic' shuffles IN DINING CAR TOO and I 'should stop it', going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A system that cools and regulates the air temperature in a room controls its heat.

clue.text: Forward-looking contributor to a big shot?

definitions.text: Forward-looking contributor to a big shot?

parts.words: Forward-looking contributor to a big shot?
parts.note: a camera attachment that looks forward and helps take a broad photograph, a big shot
